info.text: Unit 21 — Coordinating a functional/operational test. Listening, reading, use of English and vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Before the test continues, what does B fit on the other hydraulic system?

generalfeedback.text: B asks, "Should I fit the lockout on the other system before we continue?" and A agrees. The lockout tag stops anyone pressurising the system by accident.

feedback.text: Correct. B fits the lockout tag in case somebody pressurises the system accidentally.
No. No component is replaced during the brief; the actuator is only tested.

answer.text: A placard on the flap lever

feedback.text: Not here. A placard is fitted later, only after the test fails.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The limit switch made at the fifteen setting, and the indication light was green.

generalfeedback.text: B reports: "The limit switch made at fifteen, and the indication light is green." "Made" means the switch closed and confirmed the position.

feedback.text: Correct — the switch made at fifteen with a green indication.
Listen again: B clearly confirms the switch made at fifteen with a green light.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. At which flap setting (in the number of degrees called) did the limit switch make? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: The caller says "Flaps to fifteen", and B confirms the limit switch made at fifteen. The answer is 15.

feedback.text: Correct — the switch made at the fifteen setting.
Not quite. The caller says "Flaps to fifteen" and B confirms the switch made there.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 again (the voicemail). What is the snag number raised in the tech log? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: Rihards says: "I raised a snag in the tech log, number four four seven one." The answer is 4471.

feedback.text: Correct — snag number 4471.
Listen to the digits again: "four four seven one" = 4471.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. Why does the test fail?

generalfeedback.text: At full deflection the left flap lags the right by several degrees. That is visible asymmetry, and the AMM allows none, so the test fails.

answer.text: The left flap lags the right.

feedback.text: Correct. The left flap trails at full deflection — visible asymmetry.

answer.text: The hydraulic pressure dropped below normal.

feedback.text: No. The pressure stays normal throughout; the problem is asymmetry.

answer.text: The limit switch never made at any stop.

feedback.text: No. The switch does make; it may be late, but the stated fail cause is asymmetry.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 again (the voicemail). The lockout tag has now been removed from the green system.

generalfeedback.text: The voicemail says "The lockout tag is still fitted on the green system" and asks the next shift not to pressurise it. It has not been removed.

feedback.text: No — the tag is still fitted, because the aircraft stays unserviceable.
Correct — the lockout tag is still fitted.

name.text: L7 · Dialogue 2 — number of settings called

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. How many flap settings does the caller name before "Flaps up"? Write the number.

generalfeedback.text: The caller names three settings — five, fifteen, and full deflection — before selecting flaps up. The answer is 3.

feedback.text: Correct — five, fifteen, and full.
Count them: five, fifteen, full = 3 settings before "Flaps up".

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL entry, then answer.

MEL 27-51 — Flap Position Indication. One flap position indicator may be inoperative provided the flap system passes a functional test before each flight and the flight crew is advised. Repair interval: Category C (10 days).

Under this MEL, what must happen before each flight?

generalfeedback.text: The MEL allows dispatch only "provided the flap system passes a functional test before each flight". The functional test is the condition.

feedback.text: Correct — the flap system must pass a functional test before each flight.

answer.text: Both flap position indicators must be replaced.

feedback.text: No. The MEL permits one indicator to be inoperative; it does not require replacement.

answer.text: The repair interval must be extended to ten days.

feedback.text: No. Category C simply allows up to 10 days for the repair; it is not a pre-flight action.

questiontext.text:
Read the BITE readout, then answer.

BITE MENU 3 — FLAP. LH ACTUATION CHANNEL — FAULT 27-51-34. RH ACTUATION CHANNEL — NORMAL. LIMIT SW LH — LATE. RECOMMENDED: INSPECT LH ACTUATOR AND WIRING.

The readout reports the right (RH) actuation channel as normal.

generalfeedback.text: The readout shows "RH ACTUATION CHANNEL — NORMAL"; the fault is on the left (LH) channel, with a late left limit switch.

feedback.text: Correct — the right channel is normal; only the left channel has a fault.
Read again: "RH ACTUATION CHANNEL — NORMAL." The right channel is normal.

questiontext.text:
Read the service bulletin, then answer.

SB A27-042 — Flap Actuator, Left. Operators must inspect the left flap actuator attachment bolts within 200 flight hours. If asymmetry is reported, inspect before further flight.

If flap asymmetry is reported, when must the inspection happen?

generalfeedback.text: The bulletin sets a routine limit of 200 flight hours, but adds that a reported asymmetry brings the inspection forward — "inspect before further flight".

feedback.text: Correct — a reported asymmetry requires inspection before further flight.

answer.text: Only at the next scheduled maintenance check.

feedback.text: No. Waiting for the next check ignores the "before further flight" clause.

answer.text: Any time within the next 200 flight hours.

feedback.text: No. The 200-hour limit is the routine case; a reported asymmetry overrides it.

questiontext.text:
Read the work order note, then answer.

WORK ORDER 7788. Do not pressurise the green hydraulic system until this work order is closed. Keep clearance from the flaps at all times.

You may pressurise the green system while the work order is still open.

generalfeedback.text: The note gives a direct order: "Do not pressurise the green hydraulic system until this work order is closed." Open work order means no pressurising.

feedback.text: No. The order forbids pressurising until the work order is closed.
Correct — do not pressurise until the work order is closed.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite as a short safety warning (imperative). Use the base verb, no subject.

You must not touch the actuator. → ______

generalfeedback.text: A negative order uses "Do not" + base verb, with no subject: Do not touch the actuator. "Don't touch the actuator" is also correct.

feedback.text: Correct — "Do not" + base verb, no subject.
Correct.
Correct — the contraction is fine.
Correct.
Use "Do not + base verb" with no subject: Do not touch the actuator.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite as a short order (imperative).

It is necessary to fit a lockout. → ______

generalfeedback.text: Drop "It is necessary to" and use the bare base verb: Fit a lockout. "Fit the lockout" is also accepted.

feedback.text: Correct — base verb only.
Correct.
Correct.
Correct.
Use the base verb with no subject: Fit a lockout.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite as a short order (imperative).

You should keep clearance. → ______

generalfeedback.text: Drop "You should" and start with the base verb: Keep clearance. No subject, no modal.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.
Correct — "your" is natural here.
Correct.
Use the base verb with no subject: Keep clearance.

questiontext.text:
Write the missing verb.

When a functional test fails, we ______ a snag in the tech log.

generalfeedback.text: The fixed collocation is to raise a snag — you write it up for repair.

feedback.text: Correct — raise a snag.
The verb is "raise": raise a snag in the tech log.

questiontext.text:
Write the missing testing term.

The pass criteria require both flaps to reach full ______ together, with no visible asymmetry.

generalfeedback.text: "Full deflection" means the surface has moved to its end travel from the neutral position.

feedback.text: Correct — full deflection.
The term is "deflection" — how far the surface moves from neutral.

questiontext.text:
Correct the English. Write the whole warning correctly.

No stand near the flaps. → ______

generalfeedback.text: "No + verb" is a first-language habit. English uses "Do not + base verb": Do not stand near the flaps. "Don't stand near the flaps" is also correct.

answer.text: Do not stand near the flaps

feedback.text: Correct.

answer.text: Do not stand near the flaps.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct — the contraction is fine.
Correct.
Use "Do not + base verb": Do not stand near the flaps.

name.text: V1 · Match the testing term to its meaning

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: Keep "actuation" (the movement) apart from "actuator" (the device). Pass criteria = the result to reach; a snag = a written-up fault.

answer.text: the movement of a part when a force drives it
the device that turns pressure into movement
the exact result a test must reach to pass
a fault that you write up for repair

name.text: V2 · Match the safety/paperwork term to its meaning

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: Lockout and placard both warn, but a lockout stops the system while a placard marks the hazard. BITE is the system's self-test; clearance is a safe distance.

answer.text: a tag or lock that stops a system being used
a warning card fitted to mark a hazard
a safe distance from a moving part

name.text: V3 · Match the verb to the noun (collocation)

questiontext.text: Match each verb to the noun it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: These verb+noun pairs are fixed: raise a snag, fit the lockout, keep clearance, meet the pass criteria. Learn the whole chunk, not the bare noun.

name.text: V4 · Match the result term to its meaning

questiontext.text: Match each term to its plain meaning.

generalfeedback.text: These are the terms you use to read the result: deflection (distance from neutral), asymmetry (one side unlike the other), limit switch (end-point signal), rigging (the alignment setting).

answer.text: how far a surface moves from its neutral place
one side moving differently from the other
a switch that signals a part has reached its end point
the setting that aligns a surface correctly
